Two related slices:

**(a) Contract / freelance / fractional engineering.** Query terms: "(Contract)", "Contractor", "Freelance", "Fractional", "part-time engineer", "day rate", "3 month contract", "6 month contract", combined with full-stack / TypeScript / AI / automation.

**(b) Full-stack product engineering and technical product management at European startups.** Query terms: "Full-Stack Engineer" / "Product Engineer" / "Founding Engineer" / "Technical Product Manager", with stack keywords Next.js, TypeScript, Laravel, Supabase, Bubble.io, low-code, no-code migration.

**Bias hard toward postings dated within the last 21 days.** Search indexes run about a month stale.

WebFetch each posting URL and confirm it renders as a live single posting. Dead signatures: Ashby "Job not found"; a Greenhouse URL serving the board index instead of one job; "job board ... no longer active"; a passed deadline. Drop what you cannot verify and say so. Flag any row whose apply URL is on `apply.workable.com` — that host is unreachable for this session's browser, so he would have to apply by hand.

EggAI, Nuitée, Arize AI, HiPeople, G2i, OpenHands, Camunda, Viktor, tem, Oh, Duvo, Sourcegraph, Reedsy, Cohere, Goldsky, n8n, ElevenLabs, Musixmatch, MyEdSpace/Myedspace, Eneba, Zapier, Lovable, JobLeads, Kairos, YLD, Moneyfarm, Supabase, Satispay, Fueled, Gensyn, Mindrift, Toloka AI, Novosafe, Runpod, Unframe, neptune.ai, The Flex, Ben, Attio, Cresta, GTM Base, dexter health, Pinnipedia, Arkipel, Jamie, Bullpen Talent, Filigran, MAIA, alago, Stackgini, Cognite, ClickHouse, Twilio, Neural Earth, Atmen, Nearform, Aircall, Always Friday, Outliant.

role match 30 + eligibility & work basis 25 + stack overlap 20 + seniority realism 15 + signal quality 10. Be harsh on eligibility: US-only contracting entities, UK-authorisation requirements, or a mandatory office he'd have to move to costs most of the 25. Talent marketplaces and staffing shops (no named end client) should lose signal-quality points.

### <score> — <role title> · <company>
- **Where:** <verbatim location/eligibility sentence> · Tier 1 / 2 / 3 · Employee or Contract
- **Pay:** <disclosed figures or rate, or "not disclosed"> · **Posted:** <date, or "not stated">

- **Watch-outs:** the honest gaps.

{"method":"project_read","path":"claude/contract-search-brief-2026-08-05.md","content":"# Contract & Freelance Brief — Prabhavit Gupta
**Prepared 5 August 2026** · Target: 6-month contract / fractional engagement · Base: Venice, Italy (EU long-term residence, no sponsorship needed)

---

## 1. The headline finding

I searched the public boards hard, and here is the honest picture: **for your profile, the 6-month contract market is almost entirely off-board.** Two things came up repeatedly:

1. **"Contract AI engineer" postings on US boards are mostly W-2 staffing roles requiring US work authorization.** Example: Precept Labs is running exactly the engagement you described — *"Machine Learning Engineer — Applied LLM / Agents, 6 months, potential FTE conversion"* — but it's W-2, Pacific Time, and states *"You must be authorized to work in the US."* Rate was also only $4–6k/month. The whole first page of aijobs.com's contract filter (17 roles, all posted within a week) was US-local staffing agencies at $45–100/hr with zero EMEA roles. So the "US company that can pay a contractor in Italy" path is real, but it does **not** run through job applications.

2. **The EU contract boards are thin and mostly not your stack.** freelancermap Italy has 17 live projects total. The two closest: a 6-month+ 100% remote *Sistemista Linux — Automation & Operations Engineer* (DID srl, posted 31 July) and a 3-month+ *Elasticsearch / AI Search / RAG Engineer* (infom consulting, Roma, **on-site**, posted 3 Aug). Neither is a clean fit.

**What this means:** applying to postings is maybe 20% of your effort here. The other 80% is (a) getting into 2–3 vetted marketplaces, (b) subcontracting from AI-automation agencies, and (c) direct outbound with a productized offer. Sections 3–6 cover those.

---

## 2. Live and warm leads (checked today)

| # | Lead | What it is | Rate | Fit | Status / action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Clay community → part-time & freelance channels** | Active board for fractional GTM/automation engineers. A June listing (Carlton P.) was *Fractional GTM & Ops Engineer, $80–90/hr, 10–20 hrs/wk, "Remote (USA & Europe Only)"* — Clay + Salesforce/HubSpot/Outreach | **$80–90/hr** benchmark | **Strongest fit.** Maps directly to your FlowSpace GTM automation, lead enrichment, outbound and CRM integration work | That specific role is **filled**, but the channel is live with 7.5k members and recurring US-and-Europe fractional posts. Join, post an intro, watch daily. [community.clay.com/x/part-time-jobs](https://community.clay.com/x/part-time-jobs) |
| 2 | **Synergy Effect** (Lithuania, 20+ yr IT firm) | *AI Automation Engineer / n8n & AI Agent Developer* — explicitly "project-based cooperation as a freelancer/contractor," long-term partnership possible | Negotiable ("based on experience, project scope, workload") | Very high — n8n mandatory, AI agents, REST APIs | Posted 7 May 2026, so ~3 months old — email anyway, agencies keep these open. **info@s-e.lt**. Wants CV/LinkedIn plus answers to 8 questions on n8n builds, integrations, business outcomes, and your preferred cooperation model. Attach a workflow diagram. |
| 3 | **DID srl** — Automation & Operations Engineer | 100% remote, **Italy**, **6 months+**, posted 31 July 2026 | Not shown | Partial — Linux sysadmin lean, but "Automation & Operations" and the duration/location are exactly your ask | Worth a speculative application on the duration+remote-Italy fit alone. Via [freelancermap.com/projects/italy](https://www.freelancermap.com/projects/italy) |
| 4 | **infom consulting GmbH** — Elasticsearch / AI Search / RAG Engineer | Roma, **on-site**, 3 months+, posted 3 Aug 2026 | Not shown | Partial — RAG is on your CV; Elasticsearch is not, and on-site Rome is a move | Only if you'd relocate temporarily. Same board. |
| 5 | **n8n Community jobs category** | Rolling stream of "[HIRING] n8n / AI automation developer" posts, several per month, mostly contract | Wildly variable | High | Set a weekly check. Calibration warning: one June post (Magic1) offered **$1,500/month paid via Wise** — that is far below your market. Don't anchor on it. |
| 6 | **Remote People** — AI Engineer | Lisbon office **or Europe remote**, Italy eligible | Asks your EUR expectation | Medium — Python/FastAPI/AWS heavy vs. your TS/Laravel | Listed as **permanent, not contract** — only useful as a fallback, or ask if they'd start as a 6-month contract |

---

## 3. Marketplaces: where to actually spend your setup time

Acceptance rates and take-home vary enormously. Ranked for you specifically:

| Platform | Rates freelancers earn | Take-home | Notes for you |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Contra** | $30–150/hr | **0% commission** | Lightest vetting (portfolio + reviews), you keep 100%. Fastest to set up. Do this first — it costs you an afternoon. |
| **Upwork** | $25–150/hr | ~90% | 10% freelancer fee. Volume is real but so is the race to the bottom. Use it only for well-scoped n8n/Bubble-migration gigs where you can charge fixed-bid. |
| **Arc.dev** | $60–150/hr | ~75–85% | 2.3% acceptance, technical + remote-work assessment. Transparent pricing, senior remote LLM/RAG roles. Best quality/effort ratio of the vetted networks for you. |
| **Toptal** | $65–200+/hr | **Opaque, ~50–70%** | On a $100 client fee the engineer sees $50–70. Brand access is real but the markup is hidden and unbounded. Use as a lead source, not a home. |
| **Lemon.io** | $50–120/hr | ~80% | 2% acceptance. Skews Eastern Europe / LatAm supply, which means clients arrive expecting those rates. Mixed for an Italy-based rate. |
| **Gun.io** | $80–200/hr | ~80–85% | Strongest US-client rates, but the network is North-America-centric. Worth an application given you're happy to serve US clients. |
| **Malt** | — | — | The dominant freelance marketplace in Italy/France/Spain for EU corporate clients. Set up an Italian-language profile; local mid-market demand lives here. |

**Do in this order:** Contra (free, immediate) → Malt (Italy demand) → Arc.dev (best vetted fit) → Gun.io (US access). Skip the rest until those are running.

**One caution on the n8n Partner Program:** the tier you'd want — **Expert Partners** (system integrators, gets referred leads) — is currently a **closed pilot**, so you can't just apply in. What *is* open is the Affiliate program (30% rev share for 12 months on Starter/Pro plans) and Verified Node Partner status if you publish a custom node. Publishing a node or two is a cheap credibility play and gets you into the in-app search surface. [n8n.io/expert-partners](https://n8n.io/expert-partners/) · [experts.n8n.io](https://experts.n8n.io/)

---

## 4. What to charge

Aggregated 2026 benchmarks (Apr–May 2026 data, 10 sources):

- **Geographic multipliers:** US/Canada 1.0x ($80–300/hr) · UK 0.85x (avg day rate ~£390) · **Western Europe 0.75x ($70–220/hr)** · Eastern Europe 0.50x ($40–130/hr)
- **Specialisation:** AI Agents (general) $80–250/hr · AI Agents (expert) $180–250+/hr · LLM development $75–250/hr (+30–60% over baseline) · Prompt engineering entry $30–75/hr
- **Monthly retainers:** Maintenance $2.5–6k (15–40 hrs) · **Standard active dev $6–12k (40–80 hrs)** · **Embedded/on-call $12–25k (80–160 hrs)** · Specialist $15–40k
- **Fixed-bid:** AI agent (single-purpose) $10–45k · RAG MVP $8–35k · Production RAG $25–80k

**My read on your band.** You have ~3 years of shipping, a lead-developer title, real production outcomes (2,000 → 4,500+ users), and breadth across n8n/Claude Code/Laravel/TS/APIs — but not deep ML/MLOps, which is where the $250+/hr numbers live. So:

- **EU direct clients:** **€60–80/hr**, or **€480–640/day**. Open at €75/hr.
- **US direct clients:** **$85–110/hr.** US buyers do not expect European discounts and you should not offer one. Open at $100/hr.
- **6-month retainer framing (preferred):** **€9,000–12,000/month for ~4 days a week.** Retainers beat hourly here — they match the "standard active dev" band, give you income certainty for the contract period, and stop clients nickel-and-diming hours.
- **Floor:** don't go below €50/hr. The $1,500/month posts are noise.

---

## 5. Getting paid by a US company in Italy — the part that kills most deals

This is the objection you'll hit, and it's solvable. The trick is that you're not asking to be *employed*; you're selling a service as a registered Italian business. Script it that way.

**Your setup:**
- **Partita IVA** (Italian VAT/business number) as a freelancer — this is the thing that makes you a vendor rather than a hiring-compliance problem.
- **Regime forfettario** (flat-rate scheme): revenue ceiling **€85,000/yr** (hard stop at €100k mid-year forces an immediate switch). Tax is **15% flat**, reduced to **5% for the first five years** for a qualifying new business. It applies to a *deemed* profit: for professional/scientific/technical services the **coefficient is 78%**, so 78% of revenue is treated as taxable income and 22% is deemed cost, regardless of actual expenses. Under forfettario **you do not charge VAT**.
- **INPS Gestione Separata** social contributions run roughly **26%** of that taxable base — budget for it, it's the number people forget.
- At €10k/month you'd be at €120k/yr, i.e. **over the forfettario ceiling** — so if the contract is that size, talk to a commercialista about ordinary regime or an SRL *before* you sign, not after.

**US client paperwork (the two-minute version to send them):**
- You give them a **W-8BEN** (as an individual) or **W-8BEN-E** (if you set up an SRL). That's the form their finance team is looking for.
- Services performed entirely outside the US by a non-US person generally aren't subject to US withholding, and the Italy–US tax treaty prevents double taxation. No 1099 is issued to foreign contractors.
- **Payment rails:** direct wire, Wise, or Payoneer if they'll invoice-pay; **Deel / Remote.com** if their procurement insists on a platform. Offer the platform option proactively — it removes their last excuse at basically zero cost to you.
- **VAT line on the invoice:** services to a non-EU business are outside Italian VAT scope, and under forfettario you're not charging VAT anyway. For **EU B2B** clients it's reverse charge, plus the esterometro/cross-border reporting obligations. I'd get the exact wording for your invoice template from a commercialista — my sources were explicit on the tax rates but thin on the VAT mechanics, so don't take my word on the invoice footer.

> **Suggested line for your outreach:** *"I invoice through my Italian VAT number as an independent contractor, so there's no EOR or entity setup on your side — you raise a PO, I invoice monthly, you pay by wire or Wise. I'll send a W-8BEN with the first invoice. Happy to go through Deel if your procurement prefers a platform."*

Putting that in the *first* email removes the single most common reason a US startup says no.

---

## 6. Your two productized 6-month offers

Contract buyers don't buy "an AI automation engineer." They buy a named outcome with a date. You have two unusually specific ones — lead with these instead of a generalist pitch.

**Offer A — "No-code to production" migration lead.**
You led a Bubble.io → Next.js + Laravel migration on a live platform while it scaled from 2,000 to 4,500+ users. That is a genuinely scarce credential: there is documented 2026 demand from companies that hit Bubble's ceiling, and almost nobody has done it on a product with real users and lived to describe it. Package it: *"6-month engagement, Bubble → Next.js/Laravel, zero-downtime cutover, your team owns it at the end."* Sell to: Bubble/Airtable-built startups post-seed, and no-code agencies whose clients have outgrown them (you already know this world — AliCreates, Clubee, Get2Germany, Qomodo). Anchor €50–70k for six months.

**Offer B — GTM & support automation build-out.**
n8n + Clay + CRM: lead capture, enrichment, outbound sequencing, AI support agents, plus the CRM integration work you did at FlowSpace. This is the hottest fractional niche in your reach right now — the Clay community was posting $80–90/hr fractional GTM/ops roles explicitly open to Europe. Package it as *"90-day build, then a 3-month optimisation retainer"* — which conveniently is a 6-month contract. Anchor $85–100/hr or $10k/month.

Both let you say "I've done this exact thing" rather than "I could do this." That's the whole difference in contract sales.

---

## 7. Next 7 days

**Days 1–2 — Setup**
1. Email **info@s-e.lt** (Synergy Effect) with the 8 answers, a workflow diagram, and your rate. Highest-probability single action on this list.
2. Join the **Clay community**, post a short intro in the freelance/part-time channel, and DM Carlton P. — he said he's keeping people in mind for future roles.
3. Register on **Contra** (0% fee) — one afternoon, and it's a link you can put in every email.
4. Rewrite your CV headline for contract buyers. Right now it reads like a permanent-hire CV. Make it: *"Available for 6-month contracts · AI automation & no-code-to-production migrations · Italian VAT number, invoices US & EU clients directly."*

**Days 3–4 — Distribution**
5. Apply to **Arc.dev** and **Gun.io** (technical assessments — block real time for these).
6. Set up **Malt** with an Italian-language profile.
7. Write both offers from Section 6 up as one-pagers. Do not skip this; they're what you send.

**Days 5–7 — Outbound**
8. Warm network first: FlowSpace, Urlink, UltraStrategy, Qomodo, Clubee, Get2Germany, AliCreates. You have **seven** former clients across six countries who have all seen you ship. Tell every one of them, in a single sentence, that you have capacity for a 6-month engagement starting now. Referrals from these will beat every marketplace on this list combined — and the rate is 100% take-home.
9. Build a list of 30 AI-automation and no-code agencies (EU + US) and pitch **subcontracting** capacity, not employment. Agencies with more sold work than delivery capacity are the fastest-closing contract buyers there are.
10. Apply speculatively to **DID srl** on freelancermap.
11. Set standing weekly checks: n8n Community jobs, Clay part-time channel, freelancermap Italy, HN "Who is hiring" (1st of each month — filter for "contract" and "anywhere").
